title: The Obstacle Problem Arising from the American Chooser Option: $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity of the two free boundaries (Theorem 4.9)
author: Gugyum Ha, Junkee Jeon, Jihoon Ok
work: The Obstacle Problem Arising from the American Chooser Option
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem printed as Theorem 4.9 of "The Obstacle Problem Arising from the American Chooser Option" (source0.tex lines 2996--3002, source label C1alpha free boundary), delivered together with the article's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 3004--3277 (274 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is the article's flagship regularity result: for every alpha in (0,1/2) the two free boundaries x_p^ch and x_c^ch of the American chooser obstacle problem are locally C^{1,alpha} on the open time interval (0,T). The proof is complete inside the retained span. It is not a routine exercise: the author fixes a point of one boundary, transfers the problem to a small parabolic cylinder, checks the hypotheses of a parabolic boundary Harnack theorem one by one (the two one-phase equations, the source terms, the trace conditions on the lateral boundary and the lower bounds on the distance to the level curve), applies that theorem to obtain a quotient of two auxiliary solutions that is C^{alpha}, propagates this through the level curves x_{p,n} and a uniform Lipschitz bound for them, and then repeats the whole construction on the second free boundary x_c^ch by reflecting the spatial coordinate; the interior C^{1,alpha} conclusion is then obtained by a compactness argument in C^1 for the level curves, and the arbitrary alpha in (0,1/2) is quantified at the end. The argument rests on the article's quantitative nondegeneracy estimate (Lemma 4.8), its uniform derivative estimate (Lemma 4.6), the two exact identities at the boundaries (the vanishing of the time derivative and the level-curve identity), the article's own Theorem A (a restatement, with attribution, of a published parabolic boundary Harnack inequality of Kukuljan), and the interpolated local Schauder framework built in the omitted earlier subsections. Rated H3 because the paper's introduction presents exactly this theorem as one of its principal new mathematical contributions, and reproducing it requires controlling a one-phase parabolic free-boundary problem, boundary Harnack quotients, nondegeneracy and a Blow-up/compactness passage simultaneously; it is far beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises in PDE.
